title: Questions linger after shooting
article: More details are expected to be released Wednesday into the fatal shooting of a Duncan man after a confrontation with police in a Duncan trailer park.
Family have identified the man killed as Derek Welton, 39.
Five RCMP officers came face to face with Welton who may have called 911 shortly after 6 p.m. Sunday while alone in his trailer at the Duncan RV Park and Campground.

He had a knife in hand and refused to listen to a senior officer who was trying to calm him down inside the trailer. The senior officer shot Welton after other efforts to subdue him, including use of a Taser, failed.

Many questions surrounding the incident remain, including why Welton called 911, how many other officers were in the small trailer with him at the time, which officer discharged the Taser, how big his knife was, details of his behaviour or actions before he was shot and how many shots were fired.

The dead man's father, Carroll Welton, said he is waiting for answers why police used deadly force on the 5-8, 150-pound man. He described his son as sometimes "erratic" and said police have had to respond to his home for problems many times in the past three years.
Welton was addicted to prescription pain killers, which he started taking after a stint as a cleaning person at B.C. Hydro's Stave Falls visitor's centre, his father said.
